summary: TypeSafe (jev) has NO model changelog and NO trajectory/decision export format. The API call shape is unchanged since launch: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with {state, model, questions:{id:Question}}, three question types noul/choice/score, and a Choice answer {type, choice, probabilities, confidence}. The current model is still jev-1.13.0 (aliases jev-latest and jev-preview both point at it; no preview build); the jaggedness page for jev-1.13 was last reviewed 2026-09-17. The only recent SHAPE changes are in the SDKs, not the model: Python SDK v0.7.0 (2026-09-18) switched ser/de msgspec->pydantic and added a `response_model` argument to `system_one`; Python v0.6.0 (2026-09-15) and JS v0.6.0 (2026-09-15) made `Score.criteria` an ordered sequence instead of a dict keyed by integers (a breaking change for Score, not for the Choice verdict-class or Noul shapes the town uses). Published agreement numbers are self-reported and explicitly NOT accuracy: TypeSafe's workflow evals score every model against the average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 predictions, and the home-page '193.6x faster / 444.6x cheaper' headline comes from those evals (launch blog, 2026-09-14). The most relevant published calibration artifact is the Choice self-consistency cookbook (sampled 2026-09-11 on jev-latest): raw label agreement 90.8%, rising to 99.2% policy agreement with a 0.60 top-probability 'uncertain' gate, 74.2% automatic, mean probability std dev 0.0098 -- and the cookbook states this measures repeatability, not correctness. For computer-use interop: TypeSafe is stateless, streams nothing, batches nothing, and exports nothing; the only durable artifact is the JSON response {model, answers, usage} that the caller must log (and `model` must be logged because aliases move). However, TypeSafe's own Agent Trace Observability workflow publishes an agent-trajectory INPUT schema -- instructions, every conversation turn, each tool call with args and result, the final message, and customer feedback -- and returns one of seven typed outcomes via Noul/Score/Choice questions. That schema is the published bridge between a CUA trajectory export and typed decisions, and it lines up with the town's existing cua_trajectory_mapping.md field inventory (event_name, data_json.action, data_json.step_count, snapshot).
key_facts: MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt, read 2026-09-18): the docs index has NO model-changelog page. The only changelogs are SDK changelogs: /sdk/python/changelog.md and /sdk/javascript/changelog.md. Prior trove measured /changelog.md as HTTP 404 on 2026-09-17.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/changelog.md, read 2026-09-18): Python SDK v0.7.0 released 2026-09-18. Breaking: ser/de library changed from `msgspec` to `pydantic`. Feature: the `system_one` method now accepts a new `response_model` argument that can be set to a desired `pydantic` model for additional type-safety. Bug fix: `str` subclasses now serialize as strings instead of lists of characters.

MEASURED (same page): Python SDK v0.6.0 (2026-09-15) breaking change: accept `Score.criteria` as an ordered sequence instead of a dictionary keyed by integers. v0.5.7 (2026-09-14) is the initial public Python release. So three Python releases in five days (09-14, 09-15, 09-18), two of them breaking.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript/changelog.md, read 2026-09-18): JS/TS SDK v0.6.0 (2026-09-15) breaking: `Score.criteria` ordered sequence instead of dict keyed by integers. v0.5.7 (2026-09-11) initial public release. No v0.7.0 on the JS side as of this read.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/models.md, read 2026-09-18): current model is Jev 1.13 = id `jev-1.13.0`. Aliases: `jev-latest` -> jev-1.13.0 (most recent stable, official; SDK default) and `jev-preview` -> jev-1.13.0 (no preview build available right now). Price $42/Btok = $0.042/Mtok input; output tokens FREE. Rate limits 250,000 tokens/second and 1,200 requests/minute (dynamic, can change without notice). Context 64k tokens/request; 32k tokens for `state` plus the longest question. Text only (string, JSON object, or array of text values; no image/audio/video).

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/api.md, read 2026-09-18): the verdict-class call shape is unchanged. Endpoint POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, Bearer auth, body `{state, model, questions}`. Request `questions` is `map<string, Question>`; the key is chosen by the caller and is NOT sent to the model / not used in inference. Choice request requires `criteria` = `map<string, string|null>` (option -> rubric). Choice answer = `{type:"choice", choice:<argmax option>, probabilities:{option:float summing to 1}, confidence:float}`. Noul request has optional `criteria:{true:string,false:string}`; Noul answer = `{type:"noul", noul:0..1}` with NO confidence. Score answer = `{type:"score", score:float, legend:{level:desc}, probabilities:{level:float}, confidence:float}`. Response top level = `{model, answers:{id:Answer}, usage:{input_tokens,output_tokens}}`.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/models.md, read 2026-09-18): 'The response's `model` field reports the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against a specific version, pin that version's ID instead of the alias and move to the new one on your own schedule.'

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md, last reviewed 2026-09-17, read 2026-09-18): jev-1.13 failure modes include literal reading, unreliable counting/arithmetic, date comparison, indirection, context rot, adversarial content, and contradictory criteria. Explicit: 'score levels are weak in numerical calibration' -- do not interpolate between levels to reconstruct a number; use expectation only for threshold checks. Explicit structural-invariant warning: a Noul and a yes/no Choice on the same question do not agree, and P(noul)+P(not noul) may exceed 1 (worked example sums to 1.19), so a threshold tuned on a Noul must not be carried to a Choice.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md, code comment: 'This run uses `jev-latest` on the production API, sampled on 2026-09-11'; read 2026-09-18): 8 Choice questions, 15 repeats per condition, one borderline moderation post. TypeSafe raw plurality-label agreement = 90.8%. With a 0.60 top-probability 'uncertain -> human review' gate, TypeSafe policy agreement = 99.2%, uncertain = 25.8%, automatic = 74.2%. TypeSafe mean per-label probability std dev = 0.0098 (max single-label 0.0515), 0% parse failures; mean round-trip 114 ms and $0.000046 per 8-question rubric call. LLM comparators: Haiku 4.5 t=0 = 100% raw agreement with 0% abstention; GPT-5.5-reasoning 90.0% raw / 93.3% policy; Claude Opus 4.8-reasoning 92.5% raw / 94.2% policy. The cookbook states plainly: 'These percentages measure repeatability only ... None of this shows accuracy or superiority'.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md, listed in llms.txt read 2026-09-18): a companion cookbook routes uncertain Noul probabilities to human review while keeping the underlying noul values visible.

MEASURED (typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev, Diogo Almeida, dated 2026-09-14; read 2026-09-18): the workflow evals 'assume there is a correct compute graph (a workflow represented in code) and use the predictions of the largest, smartest, and most expensive external models as reference probabilities'; the reference is 'the average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1'. The blog says this 'biases answers towards OpenAI and Anthropic's models. We likely underestimate the relative performance of our model and DeepSeek's models.' The home-page '193.6x faster, 444.6x cheaper' headline 'comes from' these evals, and TypeSafe expects those are 'on the higher end of real world gains'.

MEASURED (evals.typesafe.ai/agent_trace_observability, read 2026-09-18): the Agent Trace Observability workflow takes an agent run (instructions, every conversation turn, each tool call with args and result, the final message, and customer feedback) and returns one of 7 typed outcomes (AUTO-CLOSE, NOT A BUG, HUMAN REVIEW, PRIORITY REVIEW, FILE ISSUE, ROUTE, PAGE ON-CALL). Published Jev row: workflow 71.6% accuracy at $0.0003/case and 0.5 s, versus e.g. Opus 5 workflow 75.2% at $0.1033 / 27.4 s, Sol workflow 76.6% at $0.0575 / 40.3 s, Sonnet 5 workflow 68.0% at $0.0545 / 38.0 s. Questions used: Noul/Score/Choice.

MEASURED (evals.typesafe.ai/security_incidents, read 2026-09-18): Jev workflow 61.7% at $0.0001/case and 0.3 s (best-accuracy rows: Opus 5 workflow 66.2% at $0.0574/15.1 s; Sol workflow 62.5% at $0.0295/8.5 s).

MEASURED (jev.novcog.us.com/the-evals, dated 2026-09-16; read 2026-09-18): independent analysis restates that a score on TypeSafe's benchmark is 'agreement with two frontier LLMs ... not a measure of correctness'; notes the home-page latency pair 0.114s vs 8.566s is a 75.1x ratio while the headline is 193.6x, and that no independent benchmark of Jev existed as of 2026-09-16.

MEASURED (typesafe.ai/blog/antibenchmaxxing, dated 2026-09-11; read 2026-09-18): TypeSafe policy -- 'no standard benchmark table in our model releases. New evals will be dated snapshots and immediately retired once posted rather than hill-climbed.'

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md, described in llms.txt read 2026-09-18): batching 13 questions into one TypeSafe call is '12.2x cheaper and 10.0x faster with no change in answers'. (A prior read of the cookbook page on 2026-09-17 recorded 11.5x/9.6x -- the numbers moved between reads; cite the current index figure.)

MEASURED (this box, .agi/context/local-maxxing/typesafe/acts_replay.md, 2026-09-18): the town's own held-out replay of jev-1.13.0 over 370 typed acts x 3 repeats (1110 calls, all HTTP 200, all response model jev-1.13.0) measured q1 verdict-class agreement 0.743 against a majority base of 0.507 and ECE 0.196; q2 accept/demote agreement 0.492 against a 0.776 always-accept base (worse than the constant); q3 0.989 vs 0.995 base; q4 0.909 on only 22 records; repeat-flip 1.1-1.6%. The falsifier tripped. Caveat recorded there: 74% of corpus node bodies literally contain their own verdict word, so q1 agreement tracks leakage and is not evidence of inference.

MEASURED (vercel.com/changelog/typesafe-ai-jev-now-available-on-ai-gateway, published 2026-09-16; read 2026-09-18): Vercel AI Gateway exposes Jev through AI SDK 7's experimental `evaluate` API, naming the three types Choice, Score, and Boolean (TypeSafe docs call the yes/no type Noul). Naming variant, not a shape change.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/api.md + docs.typesafe.ai/models.md, read 2026-09-18): no streaming endpoint, no batch endpoint, no trajectory/trace/export endpoint, and no published JSON schema for a stored decision record. The API is request->response; the durable artifact is whatever the caller logs. Errors: 401/422/429/529, SDKs retry with backoff and honor `retry-after`.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md, read 2026-09-18): an installable TypeSafe agent skill exists (Claude Code plugin `typesafe@typesafe-ai`; `npx skills add typesafe-ai/skills --skill typesafe-ai`), i.e. the provider ships agent-integration guidance rather than an export format.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md, listed in llms.txt read 2026-09-18): a cookbook maps natural-language requests to calls to ordinary typed functions by mapping function names and closed-set arguments to confidence-aware TypeSafe questions.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md, listed in llms.txt read 2026-09-18): a cookbook turns free text into numeric features with TypeSafe questions and uses model errors to improve a supervised CatBoost regressor -- a pattern for exporting decisions as training features.

MEASURED (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md, read 2026-09-18): the cookbook caches every raw output to `json_cache.json` and ships it so re-rendering reproduces published numbers at $0, and records per call `requested_model`, `response_model`, distributions, input/output tokens, and latency. This is the closest thing to a decision-log export contract that exists.
reusable_assets: Choice self-consistency cookbook (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_choice_cookbook.md) -- a ready-made 15-repeat x 8-Choice-question harness with a 0.60 top-probability 'uncertain' gate, raw + policy agreement, probability std dev, and a json_cache.json replay at $0. Directly reusable as the town's calibration harness for any jev question set.

Agent Trace Observability eval input schema (evals.typesafe.ai/agent_trace_observability): instructions + every conversation turn + each tool call (args and result) + final message + customer feedback -> one of 7 typed outcomes via Noul/Score/Choice. This is a published trajectory->typed-decision mapping and the strongest available interop target for a CUA trajectory export.

The town's own cua_trajectory_mapping.md (this repo, .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/) already inventories the CUA trajectory fields (event_name, data_json.action, data_json.step_count, snapshot windows, data_images, trajectory_id, timestamp) and names the gaps; the Agent Trace Observability schema is a way to fill the `answers` gap from the decision side.

Function-calling cookbook (docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md) -- closed-set Choice questions over function names and arguments with confidence; a template for a CUA agent's next-action suggestion layer.

Autoresearch feature-discovery cookbook -- turn free text into numeric features via TypeSafe questions and train a downstream CatBoost on model errors; a template for exporting decisions as a training set.

json_cache.json pattern from the consistency cookbooks -- log requested_model vs response_model, distributions, usage, latency per call, and ship the cache so a replay is $0 and reproducible. Mirrors the town's typesafe/acts_replay.jsonl schema.
The TypeSafe agent skill (github.com/typesafe-ai/skills, SKILL.md) -- installable into Claude Code / Codex, so an agent can be given the question-type and pattern context without a bespoke prompt.

The jaggedness page for jev-1.13 (docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md) as a pre-written failure-mode checklist to test any new question set against (literal reading, counting, dates, indirection, context rot, adversarial state, contradictory criteria, structural invariants).

TypeSafe's System One adapter for LLMs (github.com/typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python) -- constrains an LLM to emit structured decisions compatible with the TypeSafe API, i.e. a way to produce comparable decision records from a non-TypeSafe model.
failures_and_lessons: There is no model changelog. Do not look for one: /changelog.md is 404 and llms.txt lists only SDK changelogs. The change signals are the versioned model id (GET /v1/models release_date), the jaggedness page's 'Last reviewed' date, and the SDK changelogs.
SDK churn is fast and breaking: Python v0.5.7 (09-14), v0.6.0 (09-15, Score.criteria dict->sequence), v0.7.0 (09-18, msgspec->pydantic + response_model). Pin the SDK version as well as the model id.

TypeSafe publishes agreement-with-two-LLMs, not accuracy. The workflow-eval reference is the average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1; the town's own replay independently confirmed q2 accept/demote is worse than the always-accept constant (0.492 vs 0.776). Never quote a TypeSafe agreement number as an accuracy.

The 99.2% choice-cookbook number is repeatability WITH abstention, not correctness -- the cookbook says so in the same section ('These percentages measure repeatability only'). Its 0.60 gate turns 25.8% of answers into 'uncertain'; that is a cost, not a free win.

No export format exists. TypeSafe is stateless and has no streaming, batch, or trace endpoint. Any trajectory/decision export is caller-built; the only contract is the JSON response plus the instruction to log `model` (the versioned id, not the alias).

Aliases move under you: jev-latest and jev-preview both currently resolve to jev-1.13.0, and a future release changes answers without any change on the caller side. A replay that logged the alias cannot be reproduced after a release.

Structural invariants are not guaranteed: a Noul and a yes/no Choice disagree, and P(noul)+P(not noul) can exceed 1 (worked example 1.19). Do not carry a threshold tuned on one question type to another.
Score levels are weak in numerical calibration (jaggedness, 2026-09-17): use a Score expectation for a threshold check only, never to reconstruct a magnitude between levels.

The parallel-questions speedup figure changed between reads (11.5x/9.6x on 2026-09-17 vs 12.2x/10.0x in the 2026-09-18 llms.txt index). Treat vendor cookbook ratios as dated snapshots and re-measure on the town's own corpus.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: A <=30-line adapter joins TypeSafe decision records to CUA trajectory turns: each jev response {model, answers, usage} becomes a per-turn typed-decision record keyed by (trajectory_id, step_count, event_name), filling the `answers` gap the town's cua_trajectory_mapping.md names, and round-trips without loss of the Choice/Noul/Score shape.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: The CUA trace has no stable per-step key to join on (step_count is per-action, trajectory_id is per-run), or the jev answer object cannot be attached to a turn without inventing fields the trace lacks.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Parse one CUA trace excerpt (.agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trace_excerpt.json) plus one jev acts_replay row; write the mapping as a JSON object; count covered vs missing fields and name each gap. $0, ~20 min.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The published Agent Trace Observability input schema (instructions, every conversation turn, each tool call with args and result, final message, customer feedback) is a superset of the CUA trajectory export fields, so a CUA trace can be rendered into that schema and scored by the same Noul/Score/Choice question set at $0 locally (or $0.0003/case if jev is called).
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: The CUA trace lacks a conversation/turn structure or a customer-feedback equivalent, or the schema requires fields (e.g. a final message) that a CUA run does not produce.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Map cua_trace_excerpt.json fields to the Agent Trace Observability input list on paper, write a one-page mapping to the trove dir, and count the fields with no CUA counterpart. $0, ~15 min.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The 0.60 top-probability 'uncertain' gate from the Choice self-consistency cookbook transfers to the town's q1 verdict-class decision: routing q1 answers below 0.60 to inconclusive/human raises policy agreement above 0.85 on the town's own replay corpus (currently 0.743 raw).
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: On the town's acts_replay.jsonl, adding the 0.60 gate does not raise agreement above 0.85, or it abstains on so many acts that automatic coverage collapses below ~50%.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Re-score the cached json_cache/ rows in .agi/context/local-maxxing/typesafe/ with a 0.60 threshold on q1 probabilities; report raw vs policy agreement, uncertain rate, automatic rate. $0 (cache exists).

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Pinning jev-1.13.0 and logging response.model is necessary for reproducibility: a replay keyed on the jev-latest alias would silently mix model versions after the next release and could not be reproduced.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: GET /v1/models shows the alias and the versioned id always resolving together with no independent release, or a release changes the alias while the versioned id remains pinnable (which is the point).
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Read docs.typesafe.ai/models.md + the response schema; confirm the alias/version contract and that acts_replay.py already pins jev-1.13.0 and records the response model; state the exact log fields a decision record must carry. $0, ~10 min.
